subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can coordinates, slopes, equation forms, and distances be used to describe and solve geometric problems involving straight lines?
in_scope_units: Coordinate-geometry recall: distance, section, midpoint, area, and collinearity.
Slope and inclination of a line.
Angle between lines and conditions for parallelism and perpendicularity.
Equations of horizontal and vertical lines.
Point-slope, two-point, slope-intercept, intercept, and normal forms.
Distance from a point to a line and distance between parallel lines.
Applications to reflections, loci, intersections, triangles, and parameter conditions.
banned_topics: Equations and properties of conic sections, which belong to Chapter 10.
Vector forms of lines beyond the coordinate methods in this chapter.

known_pitfalls.claim: A vertical line has slope zero.
known_pitfalls.correction: A horizontal line has slope zero; a vertical line has undefined slope.

known_pitfalls.claim: Perpendicular lines always have slopes that are reciprocals.
known_pitfalls.correction: For defined non-zero slopes, their product is −1, so they are negative reciprocals.

known_pitfalls.claim: The angle formula has no absolute value.
known_pitfalls.correction: The acute angle uses the absolute value of the slope expression.

known_pitfalls.claim: The distance formula may return a negative value.
known_pitfalls.correction: The numerator is inside an absolute value, so distance is non-negative.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every line can be written in slope-intercept form.
known_pitfalls.correction: Vertical lines cannot; they have equations x=k.

recommended_example_progression: NCERT Example 2 for a fixed angle between lines.
NCERT chapter summary and Exercise 9.2 for equation forms.
NCERT Example 13 for reflection in a line.
NCERT Example 16 for an equal-distance locus.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 9.1, 9.2, and 9.3 followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 9.
